## Scope and data preparation

SPADES.IND generates a categorical candidate pool (flight), selects a fixed-size
subset (landing), and reconstructs numerical variables within their original
intervals. Supply training data only. Reserve a real holdout before preparation,
binning, model fitting or guide construction.

Rows with actual missing values, textual `NA`, internal missing markers or
additional user-declared `missing_tokens` are omitted once. The same cleaned
reference is used throughout. Missingness is not modelled or generated. A literal
`Missing` category is ordinary data unless explicitly declared missing.
Constant columns and unsupported column types require preprocessing.

Examples below are opt-in and use artificial data. They are not executed during
vignette building; the corresponding small workflows are tested in the package
test suite. Their very short chains demonstrate calls, not statistical quality.

## Three complete workflows

The default main workflow uses six chains and six workers. The small example
uses one worker and intentionally tiny settings. Production settings require
validation for the application; there is no universal optimal schedule.

```{r three-scenarios}
# Run explicitly after installing SPADES.IND. Uses artificial data only.
local({
  if (!requireNamespace("SPADES.IND", quietly = TRUE)) stop("Install SPADES.IND first.")
  withr::local_seed(444L)
  d <- data.frame(x = rnorm(120), group = rep(letters[1:8], 15),
                  category = rep(LETTERS[1:6], 20))
  d$income <- 10 + 3*d$x + as.integer(factor(d$group)) + rnorm(120)
  small_run <- function(data, target, mode) SPADES.IND::spades_synthesise(
    data, n=8L, target=target, mode=mode, n_pool=20L, n_bins=4L,
    chains=1L, workers=1L, seed=84L, pairs=list(), conditional_on="group",
    fit_control=list(n_fake=30L,nrounds=3L,bn_restart=0L,nthread=1L),
    flight_control=list(burnin=3L,thin=1L,log_every=20L),
    landing_control=list(L=30L,pilot=10L,log_every=30L))
  categorical <- d
  categorical$income <- factor(ifelse(d$income > median(d$income), "high", "low"))
  a <- small_run(categorical, "income", "classification")
  b <- small_run(d, "income", "regression")
  c <- small_run(d, NULL, "none")
  print(lapply(list(classification=a, regression=b, no_response=c), function(z) head(z$data)))
  # These tiny settings demonstrate API use; they do not establish statistical quality.
})
```

Use `mode="classification"` explicitly for numeric class codes. With `mode="auto"`,
a numeric response implies regression. With `target=NULL, mode="none"`, there is
no response guide or response-utility objective. RF-based association selection,
the BN and the XGB plausibility discriminator still serve their other roles.
`pairs=NULL` selects pairs automatically; `pairs=list()` intentionally requests none.

## What flight optimizes

For a fixed chain archive A, let q be the fitted BN mass, p the XGB real-class
score, and d the normalized nearest-record Hamming distance. The implemented
energy has the form

\[
H_A(x)=-\log q(x)+\lambda_P(1-p(x))+
\lambda_R\exp[-d(x,R)/\tau_R]+
\lambda_D\exp[-d(x,A)/\tau_D].
\]

An empty archive contributes zero diversity energy. BN independence proposals
cancel the BN term in the Hastings ratio. Both old and proposed states are
compared against the same archive. The archive grows during collection and is
local to a chain, so this is adaptive sampling, not a claim of draws from one
fixed stationary distribution. Duplicate synthetic contents are retained.
Exact categorical reference matches are excluded. These mechanisms are not
formal anonymity or differential-privacy guarantees.

The staged API separates preparation, model fitting, flight and landing.
Use `spades_resume_flight()` for checkpointed flight recovery; consult its help
for the checkpoint arguments. Reusing the fitted model avoids refitting it.
Calling the main workflow again is not itself a model-reuse operation.

## Landing objective and fidelity

For k variables and B distinct selected pairs, the default component count is
J = k + B + (k - 1). Fidelity is the arithmetic mean of these J components:

\[
F(T)=\frac{1}{J}\sum_{j=1}^J D_j(T,R),\qquad H(T)=F(T)+U(T).
\]

Each marginal or joint-pair component is total variation distance. Each
conditional component averages within-stratum TVD with the reference stratum
proportions. A reference stratum absent from the target receives discrepancy one.
The highest-cardinality prepared variable conditions the distributions unless
`conditional_on` specifies another column. This formulation is a mean across
components, not a maximum and not a mean giving equal weight to component
families. RF importance selects associations; it does not set their energy weights.
There is no landing diversity penalty in this workflow.

Classification utility is the absolute difference between the fixed RF guide's
accuracy on the selected target and its accuracy on the training reference.
For no response, U is zero. Selection swaps one pool index at a time, with unique
selected indices but possibly duplicated record contents. The reported result is
the final SA state. An optimum is not certified.

## Continuous response: categorical fidelity, numerical utility

The cleaned numerical response is partitioned using type-7 quantiles, requesting
ten bins by default. Repeated boundaries are merged; ten nonempty bins are not
guaranteed. The response protocol reports effective bins and counts.

The pool remains categorical, including the response bin. A fixed RF regression
guide is fitted on categorical predictors and the real numerical response.
For each candidate swap, a fresh response value is drawn uniformly inside the
candidate bin. Integer-valued input uses the admissible integers in that interval.
The objective adds

\[
U(T)=\frac{|E(T)-E(R)|}{s_R},
\]

where E is RMSE or MAE and s_R is the real response standard deviation. Accepting
a proposal retains both its pool index and response value. Rejecting it preserves
both old values. Final accepted responses are never redrawn. Numerical predictors
are reconstructed after landing, just as in classification.

The proposal is interpreted relative to the product of within-bin uniform base
measures and uniform index selection. The within-bin proposal ratio cancels the
base-measure ratio. Unequal-width bins do not imply symmetry with respect to
ordinary numerical Lebesgue measure.

The low-level `spades_utility(mode="regression")` helper remains a fixed-numerical-
pool interface for compatibility. It is not the dynamic regression branch of
`spades_synthesise()`. Likewise, fixed-score regression in
`spades_target_stability()` is distinct. Dynamic-response repetitions should use
`spades_land_response()` with explicit seeds, preserving each accepted response.
Interrupted dynamic SA is not currently resumed from an intermediate state.
Uniform reconstruction is not an additional proven
privacy guarantee.

## Evaluation after generation

See `vignette("evaluation", package="SPADES.IND")` for fidelity, privacy,
membership inference, fixed-pool stability and external utility.
The classification paper protocol is described in
`vignette("paper-case-study", package="SPADES.IND")`.

## Supported interfaces and research modules

The supported workflow comprises preparation, automatic fidelity structure,
model fitting, flight/resume, landing, reconstruction, fidelity/privacy audits,
fixed-pool stability and external utility. Historical research-module accessors
are retained for compatibility and helper dependencies. Their presence does not
establish validation of every historical conformal, sensitivity or target-size
experiment.
